stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that did gentle stretching

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They hypothesized that the color of the drinks would affect flavor identification.

**Participants.** The sample was 70 adult volunteers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

**Results.** The group whose drinks had mismatched colors: mean flavors named correctly (out of 10) = 4.1. The group whose drinks had matching colors: mean flavors named correctly (out of 10) = 7.8. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?**

**Source A.** In a study of 350 adults, the number of stressful life events in the past year correlated with the number of colds in that year (r = +0.33). Adults who reported sleeping less tended to report both more stress and more colds.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 84 office workers were randomly assigned to practice mindfulness meditation or to listen to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day. After eight weeks, the meditation group had a mean cortisol level of 9.8 nmol/L and the audiobook group 13.5 nmol/L (p = 0.02).

**Source C.** Researchers followed 500 people for a year after a major flood. Those who reported strong support from family and friends had fewer symptoms of illness and depression than those who reported little support.

questions.stem: When the intelligence scores of a large population are graphed, they form a symmetrical bell shape. What is this shape called?

options.why: Correct. The normal curve is the symmetrical, bell-shaped distribution in which most scores fall near the mean.
The mode is the score that occurs most often.
A positive skew is a distribution with a few extremely high scores, which pull the mean above the median.
A negative skew is a distribution with a few extremely low scores, which pull the mean below the median.

questions.explanation: The normal curve is the symmetrical, bell-shaped distribution in which most scores fall near the mean.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes comorbidity?

options.text: The view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors
options.why: That describes the biopsychosocial model.

options.text: The presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time
options.why: Correct. This is what comorbidity means.

options.text: The view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience
options.why: That describes the diathesis-stress model.

options.text: The use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem
options.why: That describes an eclectic approach.

questions.explanation: Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.

questions.stem: Athletes perform poorly when they are either too relaxed or too anxious, and best when moderately excited. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.
Correct. The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.

questions.explanation: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.

questions.stem: After an infection damaged the tiny bones of his middle ear, Arun's hearing was restored with a hearing aid that amplifies sound. Which kind of hearing loss did he have?

options.why: Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Correct. Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.
Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.

questions.explanation: Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group that talked on the phone
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that drove without a phone
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments?

options.why: Correct. Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.
Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.

questions.explanation: Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.

questions.stem: Damage to a network running through the brainstem leaves a patient in a coma, unable to be woken. Which structure is damaged?

options.why: Correct. The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.
The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.explanation: The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a lobotomy?

options.text: The treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression
options.why: That describes transcranial magnetic stimulation.

options.text: The treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient
options.why: That describes electroconvulsive therapy.

options.text: The now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain
options.why: Correct. This is what a lobotomy means.

options.text: Any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder
options.why: That describes psychotropic medication.

questions.explanation: A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.72. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes conscientiousness?

options.text: The Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative
options.why: That describes agreeableness.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody
options.why: That describes emotional stability.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined
options.why: Correct. This is what conscientiousness means.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things
options.why: That describes openness to experience.

questions.explanation: Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes self-efficacy?

options.text: The idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another
options.why: That describes reciprocal determinism.

options.text: A person's overall feeling of self-worth
options.why: That describes self-esteem.

options.text: The belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task
options.why: Correct. This is what self-efficacy means.

options.text: The statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits
options.why: That describes factor analysis.

questions.explanation: Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development?

options.why: Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Correct. Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.explanation: Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.

questions.stem: The group that watched the aggressive adult hit the doll more often. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The behavior of an adult model and aggressive behavior are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The behavior of an adult model caused the difference in aggressive behavior
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.78, −0.86, +0.70, +0.35. Which coefficient shows the weakest relationship?

options.why: −0.78 is farther from zero.
−0.86 is farther from zero.
+0.70 is farther from zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; +0.35 is closest to zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. +0.35 is closest to zero.

questions.stem: A researcher flips a coin to decide whether each volunteer goes into the treatment group or the control group. Which procedure is this?

options.why: Random sampling is the selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.
Correct. Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.
A representative sample is a sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from.
Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.

questions.explanation: Random assignment is the placing of participants in experimental conditions by chance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension?

options.why: Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Correct. Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.explanation: Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes contact comfort?

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion
options.why: That describes anxious attachment.

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return
options.why: That describes avoidant attachment.

options.text: The comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding
options.why: Correct. This is what contact comfort means.

options.text: The distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months
options.why: That describes separation anxiety.

questions.explanation: Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.

questions.stem: After surgery, a patient remembers his childhood but cannot form any new memories of people he meets. Which structure was most likely removed?

options.why: Correct. The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.
The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.

questions.explanation: The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.

questions.stem: Students who sleep after studying remember more than students who stay awake for the same time. This finding best supports which function of sleep?

options.why: The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.
Correct. Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.

questions.explanation: Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted?

options.why: The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.
Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.
Correct. The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.explanation: The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: After spinning on a ride, Zoe feels dizzy because the fluid in her inner ear is still moving. Which sense is affected?

options.why: Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
Correct. The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.explanation: The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the tend-and-befriend response?

options.text: The positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge
options.why: That describes eustress.

options.text: The response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support
options.why: Correct. This is what the tend-and-befriend response means.

options.text: The field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness
options.why: That describes health psychology.

options.text: The negative stress that harms well-being and performance
options.why: That describes distress.

questions.explanation: The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons?

options.why: Correct. Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.
The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.

questions.explanation: Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.

questions.stem: To treat alcohol misuse, a client is given a drug that causes nausea whenever he drinks. Which treatment is this?

options.why: A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.
Correct. Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
Biofeedback is the technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them.

questions.explanation: Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the opponent-process theory?

options.text: The theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue
options.why: That describes the trichromatic theory.

options.text: The inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage
options.why: That describes prosopagnosia.

options.text: The ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it
options.why: That describes blindsight.

options.text: The theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white
options.why: Correct. This is what the opponent-process theory means.

questions.explanation: The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.

questions.stem: Drugs that block dopamine receptors reduce the symptoms of schizophrenia. This finding supports which of the following?

options.why: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.
Correct. The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

questions.explanation: The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: The group that was first asked to sign the petition
options.why: This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

options.text: The group that was only asked to display the sign
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: After solving ten math problems with one formula, Abby keeps trying that formula on a problem that needs a different approach. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.
Convergent thinking is thinking that narrows the possibilities down to the single best answer.
Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.

questions.explanation: A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Consent is obtained before the study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Replication is repeating a study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: While counting basketball passes in a video, half of the viewers fail to see a person in a gorilla suit walk through the game. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Change blindness is the failure to notice that something in the environment has changed.
Bottom-up processing is perception that starts with the raw sensory input and builds up to a complete picture.
Correct. Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.
A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.

questions.explanation: Inattentional blindness is the failure to notice a visible object because attention is directed elsewhere.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a meta-analysis?

options.text: The bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client
options.why: That describes the therapeutic alliance.

options.text: The choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values
options.why: That describes evidence-based practice.

options.text: A statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion
options.why: Correct. This is what a meta-analysis means.

options.text: The movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care
options.why: That describes deinstitutionalization.

questions.explanation: A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a prototype?

options.text: The changing of an existing schema to fit new information
options.why: That describes accommodation.

options.text: The interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema
options.why: That describes assimilation.

options.text: A mental framework that organizes and interprets information
options.why: That describes a schema.

options.text: The best or most typical example of a category
options.why: Correct. This is what a prototype means.

questions.explanation: A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.

questions.stem: A crawling infant refuses to cross a sheet of glass over what looks like a steep drop. Which apparatus is being used?

options.why: Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.
Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.
A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
Correct. The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.

questions.explanation: The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a gender role?

options.text: The socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman
options.why: That describes gender.

options.text: The direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction
options.why: That describes sexual orientation.

options.text: The set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women
options.why: Correct. This is what a gender role means.

options.text: A person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination
options.why: That describes gender identity.

questions.explanation: A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.80. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration?

options.why: Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Correct. Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.
Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.
Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.

questions.explanation: Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation?

options.why: Correct. A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Taijin kyofusho is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others.
Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.
Ataque de nervios is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly among people of Caribbean descent, marked by shouting, crying and a feeling of being out of control.

questions.explanation: A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: A case study examines one individual in depth.
No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Jon feels dissatisfied with his running times after comparing himself with the fastest runner on the team. Which process is this?

options.why: An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.
The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.
Correct. Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.

questions.explanation: Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the refractory period?

options.text: The rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all
options.why: That describes the all-or-nothing principle.

options.text: The brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again
options.why: Correct. This is what the refractory period means.

options.text: The change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative
options.why: That describes depolarization.

options.text: The level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire
options.why: That describes the threshold.

questions.explanation: The refractory period is the brief pause after a neuron fires during which it cannot fire again.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a social trap?

options.text: A shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them
options.why: That describes a superordinate goal.

options.text: The cultural pattern that gives priority to the goals of the group and defines identity by group membership
options.why: That describes collectivism.

options.text: The view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities
options.why: That describes multiculturalism.

options.text: A situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone
options.why: Correct. This is what a social trap means.

questions.explanation: A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.stem: Walking to the phone, Rosa repeats a number again and again so that she does not forget it. Which technique is she using?

options.why: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Correct. Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.stem: In a photo of a pebble beach, the nearby stones look distinct while the distant ones blur into a smooth surface. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Correct. Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.
Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.
Convergence is the binocular depth cue based on how far the eyes turn inward to focus on a near object.
Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.

questions.explanation: Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes stimulus generalization?

options.text: The pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus
options.why: That describes higher-order conditioning.

options.text: The weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone
options.why: That describes extinction.

options.text: In classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned
options.why: That describes acquisition.

options.text: The tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus
options.why: Correct. This is what stimulus generalization means.

questions.explanation: Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
Debriefing happens after the study.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely?

options.why: Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
Correct. A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.

questions.explanation: A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.stem: A child gets out of bed during deep sleep, walks to the kitchen, and remembers nothing in the morning. Which sleep disorder is this?

options.why: REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.
Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.
Correct. Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.
Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.

questions.explanation: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.stem: On the way home, Lin remembers that she must stop to buy milk. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Correct. Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.explanation: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.

questions.stem: Without considering any alternatives, Ravi plans to join the family business because his parents always expected it. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Correct. Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.
Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.

questions.explanation: Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Debriefing happens after the study.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Ben is tormented by constant worry and feels miserable most of the day. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: Correct. Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.
Dysfunction is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior interferes with daily life, such as work and relationships.
Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.

questions.explanation: Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disruption of older memories by new learning?

options.why: Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.
Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.
Correct. Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.
Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.

questions.stem: A researcher records how many hours of sleep 200 students get and their test scores, then checks whether the two are related. Which research method is this?

options.why: A hypothesis is a testable prediction about the relationship between variables.
Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.
Correct. A correlational study is the research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either.
An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.

questions.explanation: A correlational study is the research method that measures two variables to see how they are related, without manipulating either.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent?

options.why: Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.
Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.
Correct. Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.
Informed consent is the agreement of participants to take part after they have been told what a study involves.

questions.explanation: Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes extrinsic motivation?

options.text: A conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features
options.why: That describes an approach-avoidance conflict.

options.text: The desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment
options.why: Correct. This is what extrinsic motivation means.

options.text: A conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options
options.why: That describes an approach-approach conflict.

options.text: A conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options
options.why: That describes an avoidance-avoidance conflict.

questions.explanation: Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.why: Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: After losing his home in a flood, Jay copes, rebuilds and returns to his normal level of functioning. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.
Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive.
Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.
Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.

questions.explanation: Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The type of injection given after drinking
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: A therapist keeps a client's records confidential and lets the client decide whether to continue treatment. Which ethical principle is he following?

options.why: Integrity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be honest and accurate.

options.text: Respect for people's rights and dignity
options.why: Correct. Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.
Fidelity is the ethical principle that psychologists must be trustworthy and keep their professional promises.
Nonmaleficence is the ethical principle that psychologists must avoid doing harm.

questions.explanation: Respect for people's rights and dignity is the ethical principle that psychologists must protect privacy, confidentiality and the right of people to make their own choices.

questions.stem: Eight-year-old Max cannot stay seated, blurts out answers and loses focus within minutes, far more than other children his age. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Correct. Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Autism spectrum disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by difficulties with social communication and by repetitive behaviors or narrow interests.
Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.

questions.explanation: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them?

options.why: Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.
Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.
Correct. The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
The personal fable is the belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them.

questions.explanation: The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it?

options.why: Correct. Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The amount of sleep and reaction time are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The amount of sleep caused the difference in reaction time
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Told that a stranger is quiet and loves poetry, people guess she is a literature professor rather than a truck driver, although there are far more truck drivers. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.
Correct. The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.
The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.
Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.

questions.explanation: The representativeness heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.why: A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: Correct. A negative correlation means the two measures tend to move in opposite directions.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: That would be a positive correlation.

questions.explanation: A negative correlation means the two measures tend to move in opposite directions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes cognitive-behavioral therapy?

options.text: The therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior
options.why: Correct. This is what cognitive-behavioral therapy means.

options.text: The therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder
options.why: That describes dialectical behavior therapy.

options.text: The technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones
options.why: That describes cognitive restructuring.

options.text: The pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression
options.why: That describes the cognitive triad.

questions.explanation: Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.

questions.stem: A sixteen-year-old tries out different friend groups, styles and beliefs to decide what kind of person she wants to be. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.
Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.
Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Correct. Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.

questions.explanation: Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning?

options.why: The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
Correct. The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes grammar?

options.text: The rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences
options.why: That describes semantics.

options.text: The whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate
options.why: Correct. This is what grammar means.

options.text: The rules for ordering words into sentences
options.why: That describes syntax.

options.text: The smallest unit of language that carries meaning
options.why: That describes a morpheme.

questions.explanation: Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 10. About what percentage of scores are above 110?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. 68% lie within one standard deviation, leaving 32% outside, half of which (16%) is above.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: 68% lie within one standard deviation, leaving 32% outside, half of which (16%) is above. (90 and 110 are one standard deviation from the mean; 80 and 120 are two.)

questions.stem: From her first weeks, baby Ivy has been calm and easygoing, while her brother was fussy and intense. This difference is one of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.explanation: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of flavor identification

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of flavor identification.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Flavor identification was defined as the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group with mismatched colors named fewer flavors correctly. On average, the value was 4.1 for the group whose drinks had mismatched colors and 7.8 for the group whose drinks had matching colors, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 70 adult volunteers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group with mismatched colors named fewer flavors correctly. (4.1 compared with 7.8).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the color of the drinks affects flavor identification. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the color of the drinks. The finding illustrates sensory interaction: one sense, here vision, influences another, here taste.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: How does long-term stress affect health, and what reduces its effects?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Long-term stress harms health, but coping strategies and social support reduce its effects.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, people with more stressful life events had more colds in the same year (r = +0.33).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the general adaptation syndrome: prolonged stress keeps the body in the resistance phase and eventually exhausts it, which suppresses the immune system and makes illness more likely.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, workers who practiced mindfulness meditation had lower cortisol levels (9.8) than workers who listened to an audiobook (13.5).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through emotion-focused coping: meditation manages the emotional and physical reaction to stress, which lowers the body's stress-hormone response.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
